key_insight: Random data splits can reward memorisation of duplicated perovskite solar-cell recipes rather than generalisation to new institutions and future discoveries.
engineering_relevance: Provenance-grouped evaluation can help engineers select models for genuinely new device designs while accounting for chemistry, architecture and fabrication.
method: Map institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Use hierarchical grouped splits to isolate duplicate devices, publications and institutions.
Benchmark 13 models and analyse feature importance.
evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another; tree ensembles lead on random splits, while composition-aware neural architectures excel on unseen institutions and future discoveries.
watch_item: Reliable grouped evaluation depends on accurate provenance metadata and consistent identification of duplicate recipes.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
